units.text: Yes, your spouse may be eligible for benefits on your record.
supporting_chunk_ids: Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration#1_0::c0000
units.reason: The context states that a spouse may be able to get retirement benefits if conditions are met.

units.text: A spouse can receive retirement benefits if they are at least 62 years old and you are receiving retirement or disability benefits.
supporting_chunk_ids: Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration#1_0::c0000
units.reason: The context explicitly states this eligibility condition.

units.text: They can also qualify at any age if they are caring for your child who is also receiving benefits.
supporting_chunk_ids: Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration#1_0::c0000
units.reason: The context states that a spouse can receive benefits at any age if caring for a child receiving benefits.

units.text: The amount they receive depends on factors like their age and your full retirement benefit, and it will not reduce your own benefit.
supporting_chunk_ids: Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration#1_0::c0000
units.reason: The context mentions reduction based on age and that spouse benefits do not decrease the worker's benefit.

units.text: If your child also qualifies, there is a family maximum limit, generally about 150 to 180 percent of your full retirement benefit.
supporting_chunk_ids: Benefits Planner: Retirement | Benefits For Your Spouse | Social Security Administration#1_0::c0000
units.reason: The context states the family maximum is generally 150 to 180 percent of the worker's full retirement benefit.
